title: Muse Spaces is a project tab. Connected apps update it in the background
friendlyTitle: Muse can now keep a project in its own tab
summary: TechCrunch reports that Meta has added Spaces to Muse, the consumer agent. A Space sits in the sidebar and holds one ongoing job: a trip, a recipe list, a gift tracker, a wedding plan. Meta's line, quoted by TechCrunch, is that you describe an idea in chat and Muse builds a tracker, a planner, or a project board. Connected apps can keep the space updated in the background, so a price change or a new date can appear without a fresh question. On Friday, Mark Zuckerberg posted on X that he had made a barbecue game, an event tracker, and a home-control dashboard by telling Muse what he needed. TechCrunch does not give a country list for this launch. Spaces is the second Muse addition in a week, after the video-call feature reported on Thursday.

whyItMatters: A tab is useful if the job lasts more than one chat. The part to decide before you connect an app is the background update: the space keeps reading that account after you close the window. A dashboard Zuckerberg built is an example, not a template that will run your house. Start with one list you already keep, and see whether the tab is easier than the note.
